planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Papa Goose establishes readily and settles into a dependable, wide-spreading garden performer within a season or two.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; Papa Goose bears large coral-pink blooms with a darker pink eye and distinctively curled petals and sepals on branched scapes in early-to-midseason. It won the Lenington All-American Award, recognizing its reliable performance across a wide range of climates. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous bloom production.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Tidewater Elf is a dormant-foliage cultivar that performs reliably across a wide range of climates and soils.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Tidewater Elf produces clear golden-yellow blooms with a tangerine and chartreuse throat on tall, well-branched scapes carrying 16 to 20 buds in midseason. It won the Lenington All-American Award for its wide-area garden performance, following earlier Honorable Mention and Award of Merit recognition. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to keep bloom counts high.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; this unusual-form cultivar rewards close viewing with its pinched, curled segments and reblooms later in the season.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; White Eyes Pink Dragon is a fragrant, tetraploid unusual-form (crispate) daylily with rose-pink, white-watermarked blooms whose petals and sepals pinch and curl dramatically. It carries heavy bud counts on well-branched scapes and reblooms through midseason, and it won the Lenington All-American Award for consistent performance across regions. Deadhead spent scapes and divide crowded clumps every few years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; this compact, heavily ruffled miniature forms a dense, semi-evergreen clump well suited to borders and small-space plantings.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Lillian's Pretty and Prissy bears small, heavily ruffled dark-pink blooms with a multicolored eyezone over a green throat and a white edge on the sepals, in mid-to-late season on a compact, semi-evergreen plant. It won the Donn Fischer Memorial Cultivar Award, given to the most outstanding registered miniature (under 3 inches) daylily. Divide clumps every few years in spring to maintain dense, floriferous growth.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Victorian Lace is a vigorous, evergreen tetraploid that rebounds reliably through warm-season flushes of bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Victorian Lace produces porcelain-pink blooms edged in a braided gold band above a green throat, blooming early-to-midseason with dependable rebloom. It won the Lenington All-American Award for strong, wide-area garden performance and remains a fragrant, evergreen tetraploid standard. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Trahlyta is a fragrant, dormant diploid that has remained a long-popular garden performer since its 1982 introduction.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Trahlyta bears strongly fragrant, greyed-violet blooms with a dark purple eyezone and green throat on dormant, diploid plants that rebloom reliably. It won the Lenington All-American Award for consistent performance across a wide range of garden climates. Divide crowded clumps every few years in spring to maintain strong flowering.
